record.title: BATON reports gains from balancing feedback attribution and trajectory mass in agent RL
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces BATON, which combines Bayesian Feedback Attribution within trajectories with equal-mass aggregation across trajectories. On Qwen2.5-Instruct models, the authors report gains over matched GRPO and GiGPO variants on ALFWorld, WebShop and seven-dataset search-augmented QA; a 2×2 ablation reports gains from each component separately. For example, ALFWorld success with Qwen2.5-1.5B rises from 72.9% to 85.6% for GRPO and from 86.8% to 94.1% for GiGPO. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced. The authors explicitly say the feedback likelihood measures model-based compatibility rather than causal effects of counterfactual actions.
organizations: University of Science and Technology of China

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper defines BATON as Bayesian Feedback Attribution (BFA), which reweights action contributions within a trajectory using model likelihoods of observed environment feedback, combined with Trajectory Mass Normalization (TMN), which gives each complete trajectory equal outer objective mass. The authors state that BFA measures model-based feedback compatibility, not causal effects of counterfactual actions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: With Qwen2.5-Instruct, the paper reports improvements over matched GRPO and GiGPO variants on ALFWorld, WebShop and seven search-augmented QA datasets. For ALFWorld at 1.5B, GRPO success is reported as 72.9% baseline and 85.6% with BATON; GiGPO is 86.8% and 94.1%. The setup says matched variants share checkpoint, rollout budget, reward/advantage construction, optimization settings and evaluation protocol.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A reported 2×2 ablation separates BFA and TMN. On ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-1.5B, GRPO is reported at 72.9% baseline, 84.1% with BFA, 82.4% with TMN and 85.6% with both; GiGPO is 86.8%, 93.4%, 90.7% and 94.1%, respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For ALFWorld evaluation with Qwen2.5-1.5B, the paper reports lower mean actions and generated tokens at update 150: GRPO changes from 21.51 actions/1,734 tokens to 16.39/1,301; GiGPO changes from 13.51/1,431 to 10.82/746. These are author-reported evaluation measurements.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported gains, ablation and trajectory-cost results come from one author preprint; no independent reproduction was located or run.
The inspected experiments use Qwen2.5-Instruct at 1.5B/3B/7B and ALFWorld, WebShop and search-augmented QA; evidence for other model families, environments and deployment outcomes is absent.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains replicate, two simple objective changes could improve multi-turn agent training and reduce action/token use across several task types. The current evidence is one author preprint using Qwen2.5 and selected benchmarks, so the consequence is meaningful but not evidence of general agent capability or deployment benefit.
limitations: All measured outcomes are paper-reported; this activation did not reproduce them.
BFA uses model likelihood compatibility for observed feedback; the paper explicitly says this does not measure causal effects of counterfactual actions.
The evaluated backbones and tasks are limited to Qwen2.5-Instruct and the reported benchmark settings; no deployment benefit is established.
organizations: University of Science and Technology of China
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces BATON, which combines Bayesian Feedback Attribution within trajectories with equal-mass aggregation across trajectories. On Qwen2.5-Instruct models, the authors report gains over matched GRPO and GiGPO variants on ALFWorld, WebShop and seven-dataset search-augmented QA; a 2×2 ablation reports gains from each component separately. For example, ALFWorld success with Qwen2.5-1.5B rises from 72.9% to 85.6% for GRPO and from 86.8% to 94.1% for GiGPO. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced. The authors explicitly say the feedback likelihood measures model-based compatibility rather than causal effects of counterfactual actions.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report gains over matched GRPO/GiGPO on ALFWorld, WebShop and seven-dataset search QA, independent BFA/TMN gains in a 2×2 ablation, and reduced action/token counts in ALFWorld evaluation.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint reports a matched experimental design, a component ablation and benchmark outcomes. These are author-reported claims; no independent implementation or reproduction was performed.
technical.implementation_status: A method is described in the primary preprint; this review did not inspect or execute a released implementation.
technical.mechanism: BFA forms a feedback-conditioned weight by comparing model likelihoods of observed feedback for the executed action and a policy-sampled alternative, normalizes weights within each trajectory, and detaches them from the host loss. TMN averages valid policy terms per trajectory and then averages trajectories equally.
technical.regime: Qwen2.5-Instruct at 1.5B/7B for ALFWorld and WebShop and 3B/7B for search-augmented QA; author-reported benchmark training and evaluation.
technical.reproducibility: The paper specifies matched variants and reports means with standard deviations, but this activation did not independently reproduce the code, seeds or outcomes.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched host-learner GRPO and GiGPO variants sharing initial checkpoint, rollout budget, reward/advantage construction, optimization settings and evaluation protocol.

brief.title: BATON reports gains from balancing feedback attribution and trajectory mass in agent RL
brief.why_it_matters: The paper separates two training choices for multi-turn agents: how environment responses weight actions within a trajectory, and how long versus short trajectories contribute across a batch. Its reported matched comparisons and component ablation make this a concrete optimization result to track. The evidence is limited to one preprint's benchmarks and Qwen2.5 regimes; it does not establish generalization to other model families or deployment settings.
